title: Use unvalidated v0.02 as experimental parent for v0.03
rationale: The user explicitly authorized using v0.02 if sufficiently usable. Audit shows its governance protocol is structurally coherent but not validated. Proceeding enables the first governed cycle without falsely promoting v0.02.
constraints: v0.02 remains experimental
v0.03 promotion requires its own frozen criteria and independent verification
this decision does not rewrite the v0.02 frozen contract

title: Implement v0.03 as a Python CLI/library using JSON Schema Draft 2020-12
rationale: Python keeps the validator small and portable; jsonschema provides standards-compliant Draft 2020-12 validation while custom semantic checks can enforce cross-record invariants that JSON Schema alone cannot express.
constraints: no GUI in v0.03
semantic checks must remain deterministic
dependencies must be declared
validator must work as library and CLI

title: Keep v0.04 as Spec Linter with explicit false-positive guardrails
rationale: v0.03 validated the roadmap dependency order. Its only implementation defect came from an over-broad rule that confused references with primary records, demonstrating that the linter must prioritize contextual precision and clean-spec guardrails rather than maximizing defect flags.
constraints: Do not freeze v0.04 until its rule corpus and acceptance criteria are preregistered
Require clean-spec false-positive metrics
Keep natural-language linting separate from v0.03 structural validation
no LLM or embeddings
exact spans and rationales required
existing validate command remains compatible
arbitrary semantic prose understanding is not claimed
rationale: v0.04 must be testable and reproducible. Deterministic parsing can cover the preregistered defect families while model-dependent scoring would add nondeterminism before the evaluation science series exists.
title: Constrain v0.04 to deterministic Markdown linting

constraints: post-freeze corpus hash mismatch fails evaluation integrity
post-result cases may be added only as secondary evidence or future regressions, not substituted into the frozen denominator
rationale: A seeded corpus that can be edited after results would permit benchmark goalpost movement. The corpus and evaluation plan are therefore created before implementation and their SHA-256 values are embedded in the frozen release contract.
title: Hash-lock v0.04 lint evaluation corpus before implementation

constraints: do not rewrite v0.03 frozen contract or release manifest
historical prefix mutation must still fail
repair must be covered by a permanent regression
v0.04 linter scope otherwise remains unchanged
rationale: Starting the successor cycle legitimately appends to shared JSONL ledgers, but v0.03 manifest verification assumes whole-file immutability. This makes recursive continuation self-invalidating. The smallest dependency-safe repair is to preserve historical package snapshot metadata and verify append-only ledger prefixes rather than current whole files.
title: Repair historical manifest verification inside v0.04 before linter promotion

constraints: append-only history may not use snapshots to mask rewritten prefixes
release snapshots are immutable after version promotion
future manifests should avoid unnecessary hashes of mutable global state
rationale: A historical version manifest cannot require shared source paths to remain byte-identical forever. Version-local RELEASE-SNAPSHOT copies make the prior release content independently verifiable, while append-only ledgers continue to require their historical prefix in the live ledger.
title: Preserve version-local release content snapshots for mutable shared source

constraints: JSON input only
deterministic Python traversal
no database
no network
no LLM or embeddings
no repository source analysis
rationale: v0.04 evidence supports adding machine-enforceable relationship semantics next, while databases, repository analysis, and probabilistic graph inference would enlarge the surface before the basic traceability contract is validated.
title: Constrain v0.05 to deterministic in-memory traceability graphs

constraints: corpus and plan immutable after freeze
post-result examples cannot replace frozen denominator
hash drift is a release failure
rationale: Traceability success criteria must not be adjusted after implementation results are known. The 30-case corpus and evaluation plan are preregistered and their exact SHA-256 hashes are embedded in the frozen release contract.
title: Hash-lock v0.05 graph corpus before implementation

constraints: classification is PROMOTED AS EXPERIMENTAL, not PROMOTED
REL-0.05-FROZEN-001 remains immutable
REG-0007 remains active
do not claim real-project rework reduction from synthetic graph evidence
rationale: The frozen v0.05 contract is satisfied: all mandatory gates, primary metrics, guardrails, applicable regressions, hash-integrity checks, and role-separated verification pass. The initial impact-ordering defect was fixed without benchmark changes and is preserved as REG-0007. Synthetic-only evidence prevents full promotion.
title: Adopt v0.05 traceability engine as promoted-experimental
